member.name: MarkdownRenderer.Remarks.EntryPoints
member.para: All entry points create and touch the toolkit's elements and must run on the UI thread that owns (or will own) the created elements. The theme's foreground and link colors are applied directly, while the code and border brushes are derived from the surface background on first use, so the theme itself can be built on a thread other than the one that creates and owns the elements.

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.Remarks.Interaction
member.para: By default the content that returns is configured for tooltip hosting: the viewer is not focusable and does not allow text selection, and code blocks suppress mouse selection and drag-and-drop. The plain-text fallback is always passive - never focusable and never selectable - regardless of the interaction options. opts the rendered content into text selection and keyboard-reachable hyperlinks, and opts code blocks into mouse selection and drag-and-drop. Use when an embeddable read-only code editor is needed instead, or when the rendering should be hosted in a caller-controlled container.

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.Remarks.Failures
member.para: A parsing or rendering exception makes the renderer fall back to the content as plain text, and the exception is reported as a warning through when one is configured; without a logger it is not reported. A hyperlink-open exception is also reported as a warning and falls through to the next opener, but it does not affect the rendered content. Neither path absorbs an out-of-memory or cancellation exception, which propagates. A code-block language that is left to built-in resolution and finds no highlighting is reported through the logger at debug level when a logger is configured.

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.Remarks.Hyperlinks
member.para: Only absolute links whose schemes are listed in the effective options are activatable; see for the opener callback chain and the activation contract. A link that cannot be opened keeps the hyperlink color and underline, shows the arrow instead of the hand cursor, and stays out of the keyboard tab order.

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.CreateContent.Remarks.Pipeline
member.para: The rendering pipeline is deliberately narrow: CommonMark plus pipe tables with GFM column alignment, strikethrough, and autolinks; HTML entity references such as & are decoded to their characters. Markdown constructs outside that set, including most other Markdig extensions, are not enabled and render as literal text.

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.CreateContent.Remarks.HtmlAndImages
member.para: Raw HTML blocks and inline HTML are shown as literal text, and an image never loads, so the renderer draws a text fallback. Whitespace-only content yields an empty plain-text element.

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.CreateContent.Remarks.Sizing
member.para: The returned viewer is left-aligned and clamped to and , and within a finite it is as wide as its widest unwrapped line, so a tooltip sizes to its content instead of stretching to fill a host panel; center or stretch it from the host if a different placement is wanted.

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.CreatePlainTextContent.Remarks
member.para: The content is displayed literally and is not parsed as Markdown. Line endings are normalized to line feeds like every other entry point. The rendered text is not focusable; see the type remarks for the contract.

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.CreateCodeBlockEditor.Remarks.CustomHighlighting
MarkdownRenderer.CreateCodeBlockEditor.Remarks.Resolution
member.para: Built-in resolution tries the language as a highlighting definition name with the supplied casing, then case-insensitively against the registered definition names, then as a file extension, and finally through the aliases configured in , which default to an empty map. A definition the editor engine does not ship must be registered by the host or supplied through the custom highlighting installer.
The displayed text has its line endings normalized to line feeds and its conventional final terminator removed; authored trailing blank lines are preserved.

The editor is read-only and does not accept keyboard focus; mouse selection and drag-and-drop follow and are disabled by default. The returned editor is host-owned, so a host can change it afterwards; it is the extension point for hosts that render code outside tooltip content.

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.CreateCodeBlockEditor.Remarks.HeightClamp
member.para: The returned editor is not height-clamped. When the renderer embeds a code block in tooltip content, the block is limited to visual lines and content beyond that scrolls, or is clipped when is .

member.name: MarkdownRenderer.CreateCodeBlockEditor.Remarks.WheelRouting
member.para: Wheel routing is attached when and are enabled, so the host-owned editor scrolls itself and forwards an unconsumable wheel to an enclosing host scroller, exactly like a code block the renderer embeds. The vertical scroll bar follows like an embedded block; the height clamp stays host-owned for a standalone editor.
